newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - July 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - July 8.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

The Democratic United National (Lalith) Front (DUNLF), a constituent of the ruling People's Alliance coalition, says it will vote with government on Tuesday to extend the emergency. Relations between the DUNLF and others in the coalition are said to be strained after the DUNLF leader Srimani Athulathmudali was sacked from cabinet by President Chandrika Kumaratunga.

Police arrest five suspects in the killing of a Tamil United Liberation Front (TULF) lawmaker on Saturday in the eastern port city of Trincomalee. Inspector General of Police W.B. Rajaguru who appointed a special team to investigate, said all previous assassinations of Tamil leaders, starting with Jaffna mayor Alfred Duraiappah in 1975, was the work of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) separatists.
Senior LTTE leader Pottu Amman and 800 fighters arrive in eastern Batticaloa district to mount attack on a military camp in the area, to commemorate "Black Tiger Day", military sources say.
Two new television chanels launched recently in England and France by Sri Lankan Tamils living there could tarnish image of the country, say ruling calition lawmakers in Colombo.
